Noppe.et: Late Middle High German, from Middle Low German noppe, from Old Saxon *hnoppo, from Proto-Germanic *hnuppô (“knot in a fabric; tuft or flock of wool”). Compare Dutch nop, Swedish noppa.

s: to pick or pluck off pills/nubs (from a fabric)
Sie noppt den Wollpullover, bis alle Knötchen weg sind.
She picks the pills off the wool sweater until all the little knots are gone.
to provide with nubs; to create a nubby texture
Beim Spinnen kann man das Garn absichtlich noppen.
When spinning you can deliberately create nubs in the yarn.
noppen.et: From Middle High German noppen (“to form/pick nubs”). Equivalent to a denominal of Noppe (“nodule, bobble”)
